measurement_2026-10-27.verdict: Split: BiRefNet loses to white-matte on white-field avatar material (recomposite 1.79 vs 1.08) and is the only working option on non-white-field generated frames, where white-matte fails totally (opaque coverage 1.000, corners 1.000 vs BiRefNet clear 0.975, corners 0.000).

wispkin_wan_test1_nonwhite_field_3_frame.note: no ground-truth matte exists for the Wan clip, so no recomposite diff is computed there; halo_frac is confounded on this material (skull bone colour is close to the field colour) — magenta-composite visual check shows a clean skull cut-out with no beige fringe ring; the faint smoke wisps under the skull are NOT retained by BiRefNet

backends.notes: MEASURED 2026-10-27 on this show's material (standalone ZhengPeng7/BiRefNet, 1024x1024 inference, CPU; frames, mattes and results.json kept locally at ~/workspace/mochiichao-show/birefnet-measure/). SPLIT VERDICT. (1) White-field avatar material (Dorowani idle, 3 frames, 720x720): BiRefNet LOSES to the wired white-matte — recomposite-over-white mean abs diff 1.79 vs 1.08 (white-matte scored 1.083 on the same frames, matching its published clip score of 1.08); corners 0.000 for both; belly alpha 0.996 (BiRefNet) vs 0.974 (white-matte) — the fuller belly does not save it: its softer silhouette band (soft fraction inside the +-3px boundary band 0.600 vs 0.470) and the lack of white un-premultiply cost more at the edge than the belly gains. Halo negligible for both (0.0004 vs 0.0000). White-matte stays the wired path for white-field clips. (2) Non-white-field generated material (Wispkin Wan test 1, 3 frames, 960x2048, beige field): BiRefNet WINS BY DEFAULT — it is the only one that works at all. White-matte fails totally off a white field (opaque coverage 1.000, clear 0.000, corner alpha 1.000 — the whole frame is declared foreground), while BiRefNet isolates the skull cleanly (clear 0.975, opaque 0.023, corners 0.000, skull-patch alpha 0.816 mean). Caveats: BiRefNet drops the faint smoke wisps under the skull (near-background smoke is treated as background — soft-FX shots need an eye check), its boundary band is soft (band soft fraction 0.743 on the Wispkin frames), and CPU cost is high (~78-115 s/frame at 1024x1024 on 2 vCPU; a Kaggle/GPU seat is the practical route for clip-length runs). Measured for the non-white-field role it was catalogued for; NOT a replacement for local-white-matte on white-field material, and not yet wired into generate_bundle.py.
